learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of seven component packages is ready to publish and name the gap in each package that is not, with at least 6 of 7 verdicts correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** component-package-inspector
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of seven component packages is ready to publish and name the gap in each package that is not, with at least 6 of 7 verdicts correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Reusable Component, Component Packaging, Component Licensing, Component Discoverability (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each package the learner commits Ready or Not ready, and for a Not ready package picks the gap from five. A verdict is correct when it matches the Correct verdict column in Content, and the gap is checked in the feedback. Mastery is at least 6 of 7 verdicts correct on the first attempt. Reading the package table is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A package with a page and images is complete. (2) The license can be added when someone asks. (3) A package that works on the author's computer works everywhere. **Instructional Rationale:** Judging a package against the checks is an Evaluate-level action that precedes every release. Packages that each lack one thing, and two that lack nothing, teach the learner to inspect a package item by item. **Content:** The two verdicts: Ready, Not ready. The five gaps: No license, No metadata, No README, Link outside the folder, Not standalone. The seven packages (all made up, for Watershed Basics v1.1): | # | Package | Files and notes | Correct verdict | Gap | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | watershed-reading | index.html, README.md, LICENSE.txt, metadata.json, img/ with complete image addresses | Ready | None | It has every file and its links work from anywhere. | | 2 | watershed-quiz | index.html, README.md, LICENSE.txt, metadata.json, and a script loaded from ../shared/quiz.js | Not ready | Link outside the folder | The script lives outside the folder and will not travel with it. | | 3 | watershed-sim | index.html, sim.js, README.md, metadata.json, and no license file or statement | Not ready | No license | A reuser cannot tell what they may do. | | 4 | watershed-glossary | index.html, README.md, LICENSE.txt, and no metadata file | Not ready | No metadata | The component cannot be found or described by a catalog. | | 5 | watershed-map | map.png, LICENSE.txt, metadata.json, and no README or page | Not ready | No README | Nothing explains what the map is or how to credit it. | | 6 | watershed-unit | index.html, README.md, LICENSE.txt, metadata.json, and a page that says "use the quiz in watershed-quiz" | Not ready | Not standalone | It depends on another component. | | 7 | watershed-video | index.html, captions.vtt, transcript.md, README.md, LICENSE.txt, metadata.json | Ready | None | It has every file, including captions and a transcript. | **Provenance:** The packages are illustrative examples written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The gaps follow the chapter sections on packaging, licensing, and discoverability. **Rules:** Each package has exactly one correct verdict. Two are Ready and five are Not ready, one for each gap. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one package as a file listing with notes. 2. The learner chooses Ready or Not ready. If Not ready, the learner also picks the gap. 3. The sim shows whether the verdict was correct, the gap, and the Why text. 4. After package 7 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 7 packages in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [verdict]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This package is [verdict]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 7 correct on the first attempt". At 6 or more it adds "You can inspect a package." Below 6 it lists the Why text of each missed package. **Starting State:** The first package in the shuffled order and the two verdicts. The question shown is "Could a stranger use this package as it is?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter's file table lists the README, the license file, and the metadata file, and it says links must stay inside the package.
